newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomber says attorney 'screwed up'.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomber says attorney 'screwed up'.

text.p: Convicted Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh said in an interview on Wednesday that his lead defense attorney "screwed up" his case, lied to him and should be barred from handling the appeals process.
McVeigh, who sat stoic and silent throughout his trial and has given few interviews, also told the Buffalo News he will speak at his formal sentencing in Denver on Thursday.
He remarked in the interview on his courtroom demeanor, when he showed no emotion at the heart-wrenching photographs and the tales of loss from victims' loved ones at the trial.
"I tried to be a total gentleman in the courtroom when people called me a coward," McVeigh said.
A federal jury on June 2 found McVeigh, 29, guilty of the April 19, 1995 bombing at Oklahoma City's Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people.
The same Denver jury then sentenced McVeigh to death, and Thursday's hearing marks the formal imposition of that sentence by U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch.
McVeigh complained in the telephone interview that his attorney, outspoken lawyer Stephen Jones, promised to quit the case after the trial but has gone back on his word.
"The truth is this guy only succeeded in getting the death sentence and now he doesn't want to let go," McVeigh said. "He screwed up badly, but I'm not bitter. I only want him off my appeal.
"It's a cultural clash between us," McVeigh added. "Jones would be a politician and I'd be a statesman."
Prosecutors say McVeigh sees himself as a patriot angry over alleged abuses of the U.S. Constitution by the federal government and hoped to start a second American Revolution.
In the interview, McVeigh said Jones, who was appointed by the court to represent him, told him lies. But he refused to be more specific.
"It's for Congress, the bar, and the judiciary to investigate and discover," he said. "You would not believe some of the things that have occurred in this case."
Jones told the newspaper he would not discuss his converations with his client, whom he said was "under great personal stress."

"I remain Mr. McVeigh's counsel until such time, if ever, the court appoints someone else," the Enid, Oklahoma attorney said. He said he was legally obligated to remain with the case through the first appeal.
A spokesman said the judge in the case had no comment on the newspaper interview.
McVeigh is being held in federal prison in Englewood, Colorado. He grew up in Pendleton, New York, a suburb of Buffalo, in western New York state.
